name: What Maintenance Does a New Driveway Need in Year One?

mainEntity.name: What maintenance does a new driveway need in the first year after installation?
mainEntity.text: What maintenance does a new driveway need in the first year after installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first year is important because the driveway is still stabilizing and responding to weather, traffic, and normal settlement. Concrete should be protected during curing, kept reasonably clean, and not overloaded too early. Depending on the finish, sealing may be recommended only after proper cure time. Asphalt often needs its own care schedule, and pavers may require occasional joint-sand maintenance or settling adjustments. In Los Angeles County, sun exposure and occasional rain can also affect surface wear and staining. Homeowners should ask the contractor for a simple maintenance plan that explains when the driveway can be driven on, when it can be sealed, how to clean it, and what warning signs to watch for. Early maintenance matters because many long-term issues start with small problems in the first months, such as stains, minor settling, or drainage concerns that go uncorrected. A good contractor should leave clear instructions rather than assuming the homeowner already knows the care routine.
acceptedAnswer.description: A new driveway usually needs cure time, regular cleaning, and prompt attention to stains or cracks. Concrete may need delayed sealing, asphalt may need a different maintenance schedule, and pavers may need joint-sand checks after settling. The contractor should provide a specific first-year care plan for the material installed.
